name: Höfen
kurzbeschreibung: Cozy residential community in the Außerfern with modern infrastructure and an ideal location for day trips.
beschreibung:
Overview

Höfen is located at an elevation of 868 metres in the Reutte basin in the Tyrolean Außerfern region, positioned picturesquely on the western bank of the wild Lech River directly at the foot of the Hahnenkamm (1,938 m). Covering around 8.3 square kilometres with approximately 1,250 residents, the municipality harmoniously combines tranquil village life with high-quality tourist facilities. Höfen directly borders the Tyrolean Lech Nature Park, one of the last wild, untamed river landscapes remaining in Central Europe. The natural gravel banks and braided river sections offer magnificent natural vistas. In addition to alpine recreation, Höfen is internationally renowned among aviation enthusiasts: The Reutte-Höfen airfield is celebrated as Austria's highest glider airfield, welcoming glider pilots and paragliders from across Europe.

History

Settlement in the valley basin dates back to medieval land-clearing efforts. The community was first officially recorded in 1409 under the name in den Höfen, describing a cluster of individual agricultural homesteads. For centuries, villagers sustained themselves through alpine farming, forestry, and timber rafting along the Lech River toward Bavaria. The spiritual landmark of the village is the Parish Church of Maria Hilf (Our Lady of Perpetual Help), constructed in 1692, tastefully decorated with Baroque artworks, and elevated to an independent parish in 1786. During the mid-20th century, the opening of the Hahnenkamm cable car in 1958 marked the transformation of Höfen from a modest farming hamlet into a vibrant summer hiking and winter sports community.

Getting There

Höfen offers straightforward accessibility by road and public transit. Drivers from southern Germany can travel toll-free via the A7 motorway past Füssen and continue along the B179 Fernpass federal highway into Reutte, from where the B198 Lechtal road reaches Höfen in minutes. From Innsbruck, the scenic route traverses the Fernpass (B179). Rail passengers travel on the Außerfern Railway to Reutte in Tirol station, connected to Munich, Kempten, and Garmisch-Partenkirchen. Frequent regional bus services (line 110) operated by the VVT connect Reutte station directly to Höfen within minutes.

Tips

The primary attraction in Höfen is the Bergwelt Hahnenkamm. A modern gondola whisks hikers and winter sports enthusiasts up to the high alpine plateau above 1,700 metres. In summer, the vibrant Alpine Flower Garden showcases over 600 mountain plant varieties, complemented by an invigorating barefoot trail circling the reservoir lake. The mountain panorama restaurant serves hearty Tyrolean cuisine with sweeping views extending to the Zugspitze. In winter, the ski area offers family-friendly slopes and a scenic valley descent. Nature lovers can also stroll along the Lechweg path bordering the wild gravel banks or book scenic glider flights above the Lechtal Alps.
